description: Missouri-only rules checked against the cited Missouri Revised Statutes. National rules stay in the baseline. No fines.

questions.q: Missouri's uniform maximum speed on rural interstates and freeways is
questions.explanation: Section 304.010.2(1) sets seventy-five miles per hour upon the rural interstates and freeways. The highways and transportation commission may set a different limit, but the section says no speed limit shall be set higher than seventy-five miles per hour.

questions.q: The uniform maximum speed on Missouri rural expressways is
questions.explanation: Section 304.010.2(2) sets sixty-five miles per hour upon the rural expressways. An expressway in that section is a divided highway of at least ten miles with four or more lanes, not part of the federal interstate system, with at-grade crossovers or accesses.

questions.q: On interstate highways, freeways, or expressways inside a Missouri urbanized area, the uniform maximum is
questions.explanation: Section 304.010.2(3) sets sixty miles per hour upon the interstate highways, freeways, or expressways within the urbanized areas of the state. Section 304.010.1(4) defines an urbanized area as an area of fifty thousand population at a density of at least one thousand persons per square mile.

questions.q: A Missouri state two-lane road identified by a letter
options: Is 75 mph like a rural interstate
Has a 55 mph cap, up to 60 if MoDOT raises it
Is automatically 45 mph inside every county
questions.explanation: Section 304.010.2(5) says lettered state two-lane roads shall not exceed fifty-five miles per hour unless the department of transportation sets a higher speed, and no speed limit shall be set higher than sixty miles per hour. Other non-urbanized roads covered by subdivision (4) are sixty miles per hour.

questions.q: Missouri's excessive-blood-alcohol offense for operating a commercial motor vehicle uses
questions.explanation: Section 577.012.1(2) covers operating a commercial motor vehicle while having four one-hundredths of one percent or more by weight of alcohol in the blood.

questions.q: The Missouri director of revenue shall suspend the license of a driver who has accumulated
questions.explanation: Section 302.304.3 says the director shall suspend the license and driving privileges of any person whose driving record shows eight points in eighteen months. Subsection 1 is only a notice when four or more points accumulate in twelve months; it is not the suspension trigger.

questions.q: Missouri requires license revocation when the record shows
questions.explanation: Section 302.304.7 says the director shall revoke the license when the record shows twelve points in twelve months, or eighteen points in twenty-four months, or twenty-four points in thirty-six months.

questions.q: Missouri assesses no points for a speeding violation that is
options: Five mph or less over the limit
A second offense in the same year
questions.explanation: Section 304.009.2 says no points shall be assessed under section 302.302 for any speeding violation which is over the posted speed limit by five miles per hour or less.

questions.q: For the first six months of a Missouri intermediate license, the passenger limit is
options: No more than one passenger under 19 who is not an immediate-family member
No more than three passengers under 19 who are not family, even in the first six months
Passengers under 19 only if they are over 16
questions.explanation: Section 302.178.3 says that for the first six months the holder shall not operate with more than one passenger under nineteen who is not a member of the holder's immediate family. After those six months, the limit is three passengers under nineteen who are not immediate family. The driver and passengers must wear safety belts, except on a motorcycle.

questions.q: In Missouri, what is the youngest age at which you can get a learner's permit for a car?
questions.explanation: Missouri issues a learner's permit for a car at 15 years at the earliest.

questions.q: In Missouri, how long must a driver under 18 hold a learner's permit before moving to the next license?
questions.explanation: Missouri requires drivers under 18 to hold the learner's permit for 6 months.

questions.q: How many hours of supervised driving must a teen in Missouri complete before getting a provisional license?
questions.explanation: Missouri requires 40 hours of supervised driving before the provisional license.

questions.q: Of a Missouri teen's required supervised driving hours, how many must be at night?
questions.explanation: Missouri requires at least 10 hours of the supervised driving to be at night.

questions.q: In Missouri, what is the youngest age at which a teen can get a license to drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: In Missouri, the earliest unsupervised (provisional) license is at 16 years.

questions.q: During which hours may a newly licensed teen in Missouri not drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: Missouri restricts provisional drivers from 1 a.m. to 5 a.m., with exceptions such as work or school.

questions.q: In Missouri, what is the youngest age for a full, unrestricted car license?
questions.explanation: Missouri drivers can hold an unrestricted license at 18 years.

questions.q: How many questions are on the Missouri car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: The Missouri car knowledge test has 25 questions.

questions.q: What score do you need to pass the Missouri car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You need 80% to pass the Missouri car knowledge test.

questions.q: In Missouri, a driver 21 or older is legally impaired at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: In Missouri, drivers 21 and older are over the limit at 0.08% or more.

questions.q: In Missouri, a driver under 21 breaks the law at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: Missouri sets the under-21 limit at 0.02%.

questions.q: In Missouri, how long is the license suspension for an adult's first refusal of a breath or blood test?
questions.explanation: A first refusal in Missouri brings a suspension of 1 year.

questions.q: Unless a sign says otherwise, what is the speed limit in a Missouri residential district?
questions.explanation: Missouri sets 25 mph in residential districts unless another limit is posted.

questions.q: Which best describes Missouri's law on drivers using a phone?
options: Hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers
Phone use is banned only for new or young drivers
No statewide ban on phone use or texting
Only texting is banned for all drivers
questions.explanation: Missouri: hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers.

questions.q: How is Missouri's seat belt law for adults enforced?
options: Secondary: police can cite you only after stopping you for something else
No seat belt law for adults
Primary: police can stop you just for not wearing a seat belt
questions.explanation: Missouri seat belt enforcement is secondary.

questions.q: Until what age must a child ride in a car seat or booster seat in Missouri?
questions.explanation: Missouri requires a car seat or booster until 8 years, with height or weight exceptions.

questions.q: What is Missouri's minimum liability insurance (injury per person / injury per crash / property damage)?
questions.explanation: Missouri requires at least $25,000 / $50,000 / $25,000.

questions.q: Under Missouri's point system, what is the lowest point total that can suspend an adult's license?
questions.explanation: Missouri can suspend an adult's license at 8 points in 18 months.
